Chapter 9: Saying Yes to the Unexpected
You know, life almost never follows the script we imagine. Most of us have a vision for how things are supposed to go, but reality? It’s always ready to throw in a twist or two. So, what do you do when things don’t go according to plan? Do you push back, or do you lean in and say yes to the surprise?
There’s a story I always think about—someone who lost their job out of the blue. At first, they felt that shock, that tidal wave of fear and uncertainty. But instead of retreating, they looked at this interruption as a kind of invitation. They took a temporary job, something totally outside their comfort zone, and ended up meeting people they never would’ve crossed paths with. Along the way, they discovered strengths they didn’t even know they had. What seemed like a setback? It actually turned into the beginning of a whole new chapter.
Most of us have this urge to cling to what’s familiar, don’t we? Change can feel uncomfortable. But here’s the thing: the unexpected often brings gifts you can’t find anywhere else. Saying yes—even when it feels risky—can open doors to growth, new experiences, and possibilities you hadn’t imagined.
Another moment that stands out is about a family who wanted nothing more than a quiet weekend at home. Suddenly, a neighbor was in crisis, and their plans were completely upended. It would’ve been easy to just stick to what they’d mapped out, to guard their own time. But something nudged them to say yes, to step into the messiness and help. That weekend didn’t look anything like they’d planned—but what they found was deep connection, and even unexpected joy.
We often tell ourselves that happiness comes from control, from keeping everything predictable and neat. But let’s be honest, the moments we remember—the ones that matter—often show up as interruptions, detours, or surprises. Saying yes to the unexpected doesn’t mean you’re just letting life happen to you. It’s about being open, curious, and trusting that even when things go sideways, something good can come from it.
And the more you practice this kind of openness, the more natural it feels. That fear of the unknown? It starts to fade. Instead, there’s a sense of adventure that takes its place. Life isn’t just about managing outcomes anymore. It’s about showing up, fully engaged, and embracing whatever comes your way.
